\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Rotation}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Rotation
\section{Overview}
Gaussian rotations preserve the joint Gaussian law. Their disagreement probabilities satisfy continuity, subadditivity, and equal-step lower bounds.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Rotation invariance of paired Gaussian vectors]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. For any real $t$, the map $(g,h)\mapsto(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h,-\sin t\,g+\cos t\,h)$ preserves $\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Subadditivity of Gaussian disagreement]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_subadditive}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.measurePreserving_gaussianRotation, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable, then $s_A(s+t)\le s_A(s)+s_A(t)$ for all real $s,t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Disagreement at a sum of angles]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_subadditive}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. For any measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, integer $\ell\ge0$, and real angles $\delta_1,\ldots,\delta_\ell$, $s_A(\sum_{j=1}^\ell\delta_j)\le\sum_{j=1}^\ell s_A(\delta_j)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equal-step rotation bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_div_nat}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_sum_le}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. For any measurable $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$, real $\delta$, and positive integer $\ell$, $s_A(\delta)\le\ell\,s_A(\delta/\ell)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{lemma}[Disagreement between independent Gaussian endpoints]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_pi_div_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable and $\alpha=\gamma_n(A)$, then $s_A(\pi/2)=2\alpha(1-\alpha)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{theorem}[Balanced-set disagreement on an angular grid]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_balanced_grid}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_div_nat, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_pi_div_two, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.standardGaussianMeasure}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n\ge0$, let $\gamma_n$ be standard Gaussian measure on $\mathbb R^n$, and let $G,G\prime$ be independent vectors with law $\gamma_n$. Write $s_A(t)$ for the real value of the product-measure mass $(\gamma_n\otimes\gamma_n)\{(g,h):\mathbf1_A(g)\ne\mathbf1_A(\cos t\,g+\sin t\,h)\}$. If $A\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ is measurable with $\gamma_n(A)=1/2$, then $s_A(\pi/(2\ell))\ge1/(2\ell)$ for every positive integer $\ell$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.rotationSensitivity_tendsto_zero}
